claim: Taxpayer must give the assessor written notice of objection within 90 days after the assessor mails the property tax assessment notice.
In years with no assessment notice, a taxpayer may appeal the fair market value, assessment ratio and assessment at any time, in writing to the assessor.
A written request to meet with the assessor within the 12-60-2510 time limits is a notice of objection; the taxpayer has 30 days after the conference to file a written protest with the assessor.
Within 30 days after the county board's written decision, the taxpayer or assessor may request a contested case hearing before the Administrative Law Court.
Legal residence (owner-occupied, up to 5 contiguous acres) is assessed at 4% of fair market value.
Each county must appraise and equalize property once every fifth year.

First $50,000 of fair market value of the dwelling place is exempt from county, municipal, school and special assessment real estate taxes for owners who are 65+ (SC resident 1+ year), totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind.
Failure to apply constitutes a waiver of the exemption for that year; application may be made in person, by mail with documentation, or online where the auditor has records.
'Dwelling place' means the permanent home and legal residence of the applicant.
Owner must hold fee simple title or a life estate; jointly owned by spouses qualifies if either meets the age/disability/blindness test.

SCDOR: homestead exemption is a complete exemption of taxes on the first $50,000 of fair market value of a legal residence; for tax year 2026 the State temporarily authorized an additional homestead exemption for certain recipients; apply to the county.
SCDOR: the 4% legal residence ratio must be applied for through the county assessor's office and approved before the exemption is granted.

SC imposes a deed recording fee for recording a deed transferring realty: $1.85 per $500 (or fraction) of the realty's value.
The fee is composed of a state fee of $1.30 per $500 and a county fee of $0.55 per $500.

The clerk of court or register of deeds collects the fee before recording and requires an affidavit of value signed by a person connected with the transaction (clerk may waive); exempt deeds must state the exemption reason.

Exempt deeds include: value $100 or less; transfers to federal/state/local government; transfers under IRC 1041 (spousal/divorce); partition without consideration; deeds in lieu of foreclosure and foreclosure deeds to the mortgagee; corrective or quitclaim deeds confirming vested title with no consideration; and family partnership/trust transfers without consideration.
False affidavit of value is a misdemeanor punishable by up to $1,000 fine or one year, or both.

SC mortgage foreclosures are judicial; a Master-in-Equity (or court) conducts the sale and issues a deed to the successful bidder.
After a foreclosure sale, if the debt is not paid in full the lender may seek a deficiency judgment.
A defendant against whom a personal judgment is sought may, within 30 days after the sale, petition the clerk of court for an order of appraisal.
Appraisal rights cannot be waived in a foreclosure relating to a dwelling place or consumer credit transaction.

Three disinterested state-certified/licensed appraisers value the property as of the sale date; the appraised value is credited against the deficiency, extinguishing it if the value meets or exceeds the deficiency.
The SC Supreme Court rescinded its administrative orders governing foreclosure loss mitigation in 2023.

The affidavit must state no PR appointment is pending, be countersigned by the probate judge, and be filed in the probate court of the decedent's domicile county.

In counties other than the 25 listed counties (including Charleston, Greenville, Richland, Horry), the clerk of court performs the register of deeds duties; the listed counties have a register of deeds.
Before recording, a deed must be proved by a subscribing witness affidavit or acknowledged by the grantor in the presence of two witnesses before an officer competent to administer oaths.
The register of deeds records instruments in the order presented, once execution is proved.

A corrective or quitclaim deed used to confirm title already vested in the grantee, with no consideration, is exempt from the deed recording fee.
Quitclaim deeds must meet the same recording requirements: signed and acknowledged before two witnesses or proved by subscribing witness affidavit.
If consideration is paid, the exemption does not apply; an affidavit stating the exemption reason is filed.
Property taxes, assessments and penalties are a first lien on the taxed property, attaching at the beginning of the fiscal year in which the tax is levied.
Taxes are first paid out of estate assets or execution/attachment proceeds; the county treasurer may enforce the lien by execution.
Penalties: 3% if unpaid before Jan 16 (or 30 days after notices mailed), additional 7% if unpaid before Feb 2, additional 5% if unpaid before Mar 17; then tax execution issues.
Real property sold at a delinquent tax sale may be redeemed within 12 months by the defaulting taxpayer, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor.
Redemption interest on the bid: 3% in months 1-3, 6% in months 4-6, 9% in months 7-9, 12% in months 10-12, not exceeding the bid submitted for the forfeited land commission.
The delinquent tax collector must mail certified notice 20-45 days before the redemption period ends.
If not redeemed, a tax title is made to the purchaser within 30 days or as soon after as possible.
Tax sale advertising runs once a week for three consecutive weeks for real property.
After an additional 12 months post-redemption period, a tax deed is incontestable on procedural or other grounds.
Nonpayment: landlord may terminate if rent is unpaid five days after due, with written notice (can be in the lease) of nonpayment and intent to terminate.
Other breaches: written notice with termination not less than 14 days after receipt if not remedied.
Landlord may obtain evictions in magistrate's or circuit court without posting bond.
Evicted tenant's property placed on a public street is removed after 48 hours (excluding weekends/holidays); eviction notice must inform the tenant.
Week-to-week tenancy terminable on 7 days written notice; month-to-month on 30 days.
Month-to-month tenancy can be terminated by either party with 30 days' written notice.
Holdover tenants after lease end may be sued for possession; willful holdover can yield up to three months' rent or twice actual damages plus fees.

Owner must furnish the purchaser a written Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement in the form promulgated by the SC Real Estate Commission, except for exempt transfers.

Required items include wood-destroying insects, lead paint, asbestos, radon, underground storage tanks and environmental contamination.
